# opencode-aifs-provider

OpenCode V2 plugin that auto-discovers **AIFS LLM Serving** models at runtime from the provider's `/models` endpoint, so users no longer hand-maintain a `models` block in `opencode.json(c)`.

> **Compatibility**: Tested against AIFS LLM Serving (OpenAI-compatible `/models` endpoint). Other AIFS pillars (SmartChat, RAG, Fine Tuning) are not covered by this plugin.

## Why

AIFS (AI Foundation Services, T-Systems) exposes an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint but is not indexed on models.dev. OpenCode V2 cannot auto-discover models from a generic `openai-compatible` provider's `/models` endpoint — it relies on explicit `models` entries in config. This plugin closes that gap by calling the AIFS API at startup and registering the discovered models through OpenCode's provider transform API.

## Install

```sh
npm install -g opencode-aifs-provider
```

## Configure

Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-aifs-provider"],
  "providers": {
    "aifs": {
      "name": "AIFS",
      "package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "settings": {
        "baseURL": "{env:AIFS_BASE_URL}",
        "apiKey": "{env:AIFS_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

No `models` block under `providers.aifs` — the plugin fills it at runtime.

If you maintain multiple AIFS provider entries (e.g. one per project API key), list them all under `provider_ids` and load the plugin once:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-aifs-provider", "options": { "provider_ids": ["aifs", "aifs-project-x"] } }],
  "providers": {
    "aifs": {
      "name": "AIFS",
      "package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "settings": { "baseURL": "{env:AIFS_BASE_URL}", "apiKey": "{env:AIFS_API_KEY}" }
    },
    "aifs-project-x": {
      "name": "AIFS (project X)",
      "package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "settings": { "baseURL": "{env:AIFS_BASE_URL}", "apiKey": "{env:AIFS_API_KEY_PROJECT_X}" }
    }
  }
}
```

The plugin iterates `provider_ids`, reads `baseURL` and `apiKey` from each provider entry's `settings` (the host resolves `{env:...}` placeholders before exposing them), fetches `/models` per entry, and registers the discovered models under the matching provider ID.

## Environment

| Variable | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AIFS_BASE_URL` | yes | Must include the API version, e.g. `https://llm-server.llmhub.t-systems.net/v2`. Referenced by the provider entry's `settings.baseURL` via `{env:...}`. |
| `AIFS_API_KEY` | yes | AIFS API key with model-list scope. Referenced by the provider entry's `settings.apiKey` via `{env:...}`. |

Credentials are read from the provider entry, not the plugin options — so the env vars are only required because the provider entry references them.

## Plugin options

Pass options via the object form in the `plugins` array:

```jsonc
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-aifs-provider", "options": { "provider_ids": ["aifs"] } }] }
```

| Option | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_ids` | `["aifs"]` | Register models under these provider IDs. Each must match a key under `providers` in your config. |
| `reasoning_efforts` | `{}` | Map of AIFS model ID → array of effort values. Each matching discovered model gets one selectable variant per effort (see below). |
| `cache_ttl_sec` | `7200` | Docs-catalog cache lifetime in seconds. `0` = this launch bypasses the cache: never serves it (not even a stale snapshot after a fetch failure) and writes a fresh record back. Absent or `null` is silent; invalid values fall back to the default with one error line. `/v2/models` is always fetched fresh regardless. |
| `verbose` | `false` | Diagnostic logging: lists `reasoning_efforts` model IDs that no provider returned, plus registered models the docs catalog does not cover. Quiet by default. |

`provider_ids` supersedes the former `providerIDs` key, which remains accepted as a deprecated legacy alias — when both are set, `provider_ids` wins.

`reasoning_efforts` attaches reasoning-effort variants to models that support them:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{
    "package": "opencode-aifs-provider",
    "options": {
      "provider_ids": ["aifs", "aifs-project-x"],
      "reasoning_efforts": {
        "GLM-5.3": ["none", "high", "max"],
        "GLM-5.3-Flash": ["low", "high", "max"]
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

Each effort value becomes a model variant, selected with `#` — e.g. `aifs/GLM-5.3#max` sends `reasoning_effort: "max"` in the request body.
Effort values are passed through verbatim; the valid values per model are listed in the AIFS LLM-serving docs.

The option only decorates models the API actually returns, so it never creates models. A configured model ID returned by no provider is not logged by default — that can be a typo, but also a plan-gated model or a key that filters it out. Set `"verbose": true` to list unmatched IDs.

## Behavior

- Fetches `${baseURL}/models` with Bearer auth at plugin load, once per provider ID in `provider_ids`.
- OpenCode supports chat models that emit text output (`model_type === "LLM"` and `output_modalities` includes `"text"`). Models not matching this are ignored.
- Maps AIFS metadata to OpenCode `Model.Info`: `id`, `name` (`display_name`), `limit.context`/`output` (`max_sequence_length`/`max_output_length`), `capabilities.input`/`output` (modalities, lowercased), `status` (`Stable`→`active`, `Experimental`→`beta`).
- Enriches registered models with data the AIFS API does not report, from the public model docs page at `https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/models/` (no auth; at most one fresh snapshot per plugin load, shared by all providers, persisted to plugin storage — see `cache_ttl_sec`): token costs — `inputPrice`/`outputPrice`/`cachedInputPrice` → `Model.Info.cost`, USD per million tokens — and tool-calling support, where a docs `toolCalling: false` is the only value that flips `capabilities.tools` off its default (`true`). The API remains the source of truth for everything else. The dev (`aifs-dev`) and published (`aifs`) plugin instances keep separate caches on the same machine.
- The docs join is exact on model ID — unmatched models simply register without cost data and with the default tool-calling value. A docs-fetch failure never blocks discovery: the last cached snapshot is served if one exists, otherwise models register exactly as before.
- Calls `ctx.provider.transform(editor => editor.models.set(providerID, models))`.
- On fetch failure: logs and skips — does not crash OpenCode.

# Changelog

## 0.5.0

### Added

- `cache_ttl_sec` option (default `7200`): docs-catalog cache lifetime in seconds. The catalog snapshot (token prices, tool-calling) is persisted to plugin storage (`docs-catalog`, namespaced per plugin id), so a plugin load within the TTL of the last successful fetch serves the snapshot and skips the page fetch. A failed fetch serves the last held snapshot — unless `cache_ttl_sec` is `0`, which never serves the cache (stale snapshots included) and writes a fresh record back after the fetch. Invalid values (negative, NaN, string) fall back to the default with one error line; absent or `null` is silent. A cache hit is logged under `verbose`. Scope: docs catalog only — `/v2/models` stays always-fresh.

## 0.4.0

### Added

- `verbose` option (default `false`): diagnostic logging. Lists `reasoning_efforts` model IDs that no provider returned, plus registered models the docs catalog does not cover.
- Token-cost and tool-calling enrichment from the public AIFS model docs page (`https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/models/`, no auth): fetched once per plugin load (10s timeout) and shared by all providers, joined to discovered models by exact ID. `inputPrice`/`outputPrice`/`cachedInputPrice` populate `Model.Info.cost` (USD per million tokens; cache write → `0`, AIFS publishes none), and a docs `toolCalling: false` is the only value that flips `capabilities.tools` off its default. Join misses are silent unless `verbose`; a docs-fetch failure logs one error and never blocks model discovery.

### Changed

- The unmatched-`reasoning_efforts` warning introduced in 0.3.0 is no longer logged by default — expected absence (plan-gated models, per-key model filtering, docs/API ID drift) should not spam the log. Opt in with `verbose` to restore it.

## 0.3.0

### Added

- `reasoning_efforts` option: map of AIFS model ID to an array of reasoning-effort strings, e.g. `{ "GLM-5.3": ["none", "high", "max"] }`. Every discovered model with an entry gets one selectable variant per effort, injected as a request-body overlay (`reasoning_effort`). Select via `provider/model#variant`, e.g. `aifs/GLM-5.3#max`. Variants are attached only to models the API returns — a model filtered out for one provider is skipped silently, and one aggregate warning is logged when a configured ID matches no provider at all. Valid effort values are listed on the AIFS docs comparison page.

### Changed

- Option key `providerIDs` renamed to `provider_ids` (OpenCode config snake_case convention). `providerIDs` remains accepted as a deprecated legacy alias; when both are set, `provider_ids` wins.

## 0.2.0

### Breaking

- **`providerID` option → `providerIDs` (string → string[])**: the plugin now registers models under multiple provider IDs from a single load. Migrate `{"providerID": "aifs"}` → `{"providerIDs": ["aifs"]}`. Omitting the option still defaults to `["aifs"]`.
- **`baseURL` and `apiKey` plugin options removed**: credentials are now read from each provider entry's `settings` in `opencode.json(c)`. The host resolves `{env:...}` placeholders before exposing them. Remove `baseURL`/`apiKey` from the plugin `options` object and ensure the matching provider entry has them under `settings`.

### Added

- Multi-provider support: list one provider ID per project API key in `providerIDs`; the plugin fetches `/models` per entry and registers the discovered models under the matching provider ID.
- Per-provider error isolation: one provider's fetch or credentials failure no longer aborts the others. A summary log line reports counts per provider.

### Fixed

- Plugin now defers provider lookup past `setup` — config providers are not available synchronously during setup (host activates them after plugins load). Polls the transform editor (100ms interval, 10s timeout) until each provider entry appears.

## 0.1.0

- Initial release: auto-discovers AIFS LLM Serving models from `/v2/models` and registers them under a single provider ID.
